description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/memory.rs:240

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct MemoryError(pub String);
```

Two API-contract risks bundled together:

1. The inner `String` is publicly exposed. Once `MemoryError("...".into())`
   is constructible from external callers (and it is, because both the
   struct and the field are `pub`), the maintainer cannot:
   - Add `#[non_exhaustive]` (would break struct-literal construction)
   - Wrap a real error-source chain (e.g. `Box<dyn Error>` + context) without
     either renaming the field (breaking pattern destructure) or keeping the
     `pub String` as a synthesized-from-the-source field (lossy).

2. The choice locks the impl into "all errors are strings". A future
   MemoryBackend that internally surfaces a typed error (database error
   chain, serde error variants) cannot do so without either (a) lossy
   downcast to a string at the boundary, or (b) a breaking change.

The canonical mail-server sibling (`crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:444`)
has the same shape, so this is workspace policy across the sibling family. But
workspace policy locking does not make this finding less of a contract risk —
just a wider-scoped one. Filing here against sharing-server because the
present review is scoped to it; a separate workspace-wide bead would propagate
the fix.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: a downstream consumer
writing integration tests that pattern-match on `MemoryError("specific
message".to_string())` becomes coupled to the exact wording of error
strings produced by MemoryBackend. There is no Display contract beyond
the default. Both axes (construction and inner format) are caller-visible
and immutable post-0.1.
title: MemoryError(pub String) — public tuple field locks impl, blocks future #[non_exhaustive]
